---
title: "Bootstrap the Spack Builder"
subtitle: "Create the empty Rocky 9 workshop before declaring project software"
execute:
  eval: false
---

The first container is a workshop, not the project runtime. It contains Rocky
Linux 9 and a pinned Spack release, but no project packages. Quarto
materializes this Manual; Singularity or Apptainer builds the small definition
below into `spack-builder.sif`. The cluster's Spack installation remains useful
for inspection and troubleshooting, but is not allowed to resolve this
project’s package graph.

This separates bootstrapping from project resolution. Later pages use this
builder image to handle Spack work in Rocky 9; the final runtime image contains
the resolved project view, not a mutable Spack installation.

The upstream Spack image supplies Spack under `/opt/spack`, but a Singularity
image must declare its own runtime environment rather than relying on the
Docker image entrypoint. The definition therefore adds `/opt/spack/bin` to
`PATH`; `spack --version` is the first observable promise of this stage.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm the bootstrap tools"}

```sh
command -v quarto
command -v singularity
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-generic file="{{ emit.project_root }}/containers/bootstrap/spack-builder.def" title="Emit the bare builder definition"}

```text
Bootstrap: docker
From: spack/rockylinux9:1.2.0

%environment
export SPACK_ROOT=/opt/spack
export PATH=/opt/spack/bin:${PATH}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Build the empty workshop"}

```sh
mkdir -p artifacts/containers
singularity build --fakeroot artifacts/containers/spack-builder.sif \
  containers/bootstrap/spack-builder.def
```

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Verify the empty workshop"}

```sh
quarto render notebooks --profile emit --no-execute
singularity exec artifacts/containers/spack-builder.sif spack --version
singularity exec artifacts/containers/spack-builder.sif cat /etc/os-release
```

The successful image and the two commands above are the promised evidence for
this stage: the workshop exists, runs Rocky 9, and has Spack available, but it
does not yet claim to contain R or any project dependency.

:::
